title: is meditation Buddhist?
hookLine: mindfulness before it was a corporate wellness word: the old word underneath the apps

cards: Mindfulness is on water bottles, on coloring books, in the employee handbook somewhere between the dental plan and the parking policy.

Meditation apps teach it, and some give old Buddhist practices new names along the way: insight meditation, calming meditation. So, is meditation Buddhist? Much of what the apps teach grew out of Buddhist practice.
The longer answer starts with the old word underneath, and it turns out to be about remembering.

teach.b: The old word is sati, in Pali. A Victorian scholar picked mindfulness to translate it, and the English stuck. Sati is related to a Sanskrit word for memory, so it isn't only paying attention.
It's remembering to pay attention, and not letting it slip. The old texts give it a job.

A fortress on the frontier has a wise gatekeeper who keeps out strangers and lets in the people he knows. He can only do that if he stays at his post and looks at every face. That gatekeeper, the text says, is sati.
Here's what the apps often leave out.

teach.h: ONE PART OF AN EIGHT-PART PATH
teach.b: In the Buddha's teaching, mindfulness is one part of an eight-part path, sitting beside how you speak, how you act and how you earn a living. It isn't a productivity tool.
It's meant to notice everything, even whether what you're doing is kind.
So if you already sit with an app, you're practicing something with deep roots.
And nobody has to become a Buddhist to sit: the tradition's own word for its teaching is an invitation, come and see. The tradition just sets it in a bigger room.

how: Buddhists practice sati in sitting meditation, in walking and in daily tasks, often following the four foundations of mindfulness: the body, feelings, the mind and mental patterns; in the tradition it is one part of the eightfold path, alongside ethical speech, action and livelihood.

s: mindfulness was invented as a workplace wellness tool
it's an old translation of sati, one part of the Buddha's eight-part path.
sati is related to a word for memory
the Sanskrit smriti. sati is remembering to notice.
forgetting the breath means you've failed at sati
remembering to come back is the practice itself.

games.q: you're the gatekeeper of a frontier fortress. a stranger walks up. what does the gatekeeper in the old image do?
o: let everyone through. not his business.
know who's who: keep strangers out, let friends in.
games.why: the wise gatekeeper keeps out strangers and admits those he knows. sati is that watchfulness: staying at the gate and seeing who's there.

practice: Three breaths with the bell. Rest your attention on the breath. When a thought walks up to the gate, and one will, don't chase it and don't slam the gate.
Just notice it: thought. Then remember the breath. Each time you remember, that's sati.

wordCard.voice: Sati. Mindfulness, older and fuller: remembering to notice, the gatekeeper at the gate. Third word on your strand.

orig.note: Pali: mindfulness, awareness. Related to Sanskrit smṛti, memory.

carryVoice: Your line: remember to notice. Forgetting isn't failing; remembering again is the practice. Day three.
